- agent-browser: Browse the web for any task — research topics, read articles, interact with web apps, fill forms, take screenshots, extract data, and test web pages. Use whenever a browser would be useful, not just when the user explicitly asks.
- frontend-engineer: Pro frontend engineering discipline. Enforces build-test-verify workflow for every web project. Never declare done until the site is built, tested, responsive, accessible, and visually verified in a real browser. Use alongside vercel-cli for production-quality deployments.
- onecli-gateway: OneCLI Gateway: transparent HTTPS proxy that injects stored credentials into outbound calls. You MUST use this skill when the user asks you to read emails, check calendar, access GitHub repos, create issues, check Stripe payments, or interact with ANY external service or API. Do NOT use browser extensions or OAuth CLI tools. Make HTTP requests directly; the gateway injects credentials automatically.
- self-customize: Customize your own agent — add capabilities, install packages, add MCP servers, edit code or CLAUDE.md. Use when the user asks you to add a feature, install a tool, or modify how you work. For non-trivial code changes, delegate to a builder agent via create_agent.
- slack-formatting: Format messages for Slack using mrkdwn syntax. Use when responding to Slack channels (folder starts with "slack_" or JID contains slack identifiers).
- vercel-cli: Deploy apps to Vercel. Use when asked to deploy, ship, or publish a web application, or manage Vercel projects, domains, and environment variables.
- welcome: Introduce yourself to a newly connected channel. Triggered automatically when a channel is first wired. Send a friendly greeting and brief overview of what you can do.
- whatsapp-formatting: Format messages for WhatsApp, including mentions that render as real WhatsApp tags. Use when responding in a WhatsApp conversation (platform_id / chatJid ends with @s.whatsapp.net or @g.us).
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
I have everything needed. Here is the structured research report.

---

# L&D / Corporate Learning Platforms — AI Narrative Research (2025–2026)

Research prioritized live marketing sites and 2025–2026 press releases. All quotes are verbatim.

## Headline finding on your core question

**None of the four frames a true personal 1:1 AI companion that walks an individual employee through adopting a specific change or new system.** They all launched "AI agents" in 2025–2026, but every one operates at the **workflow/organizational level** — compliance triage, skill-gap analysis, content creation, admin automation, learner nudges — not as an individual's personal guide through a change. The closest anyone gets is Cornerstone's "digital teammate" language and Absorb's "real-time guidance where work happens," but both stay institutional. This is the open lane for NanoShellano's positioning: the individual-employee 1:1 change companion is unclaimed by the incumbents.

---

## 1. Cornerstone OnDemand

**What it is:** Enterprise talent/learning + skills-readiness platform. URL: cornerstoneondemand.com

**Verbatim hero copy:**
- Tagline: **"Grow human potential exponentially"**
- Subhead: **"Insights leaders want. Learning and skills people need. Agents to make action easy.™"**
- Positioning line: **"The intelligence platform for workforce readiness"**
- Product brand: **"Cornerstone Workforce AI™"**; agent examples branded **"Embark Navigator"** and **"Skills Architect"**

**AI-agent language (2025–2026), verbatim:**
- **"a new system of learner, admin, and content AI agents embedded across Cornerstone Galaxy automates tasks, personalizes learning experiences, and delivers richer insights seamlessly integrated into the flow of work"** (HR Tech 2025)
- Agents described as **"digital teammates: personalized, conversational, and context-aware"**
- CEO Himanshu Palsule: **"AI adoption fails when it's being treated as a bolt on... this expansion of our Cornerstone Galaxy platform helps align AI adoption with strategic business goals, by offering the personalization individuals need with multi-role AI agents."**
- May 2026 launch framing: **"the insights leaders want, the skills people need, and AI agents that make action easy"**
- CEO: **"AI should bring out the best in any workforce, making them more informed, more capable and more connected"**

**Story frame:** Two decades of workforce data (45M users, 55,000-skill taxonomy, 1B+ profiles) become an "inference layer" for "workforce readiness." Problem = AI is bolted on and adoption fails; solution = an integrated "system of agents" trained on your own data.

**Emotional/strategic angle:** Scale + gravitas ("Grow human potential exponentially," "every 3 seconds"). Enterprise, data-moat, boardroom-strategic. Aspirational-institutional, not personal.

**Buyer:** HR and IT executives; **Chief Learning Officer** (Cisco CLO Marci Paino quoted); "Learning and Development Leader" (Konica Minolta). CHRO not explicitly named. Clearly a **"leaders"**-targeted CLO/exec sale.

**1:1 individual companion?** No. Agents are learner/admin/content roles serving org outcomes (goal alignment, mobility, onboarding navigation, coaching managers). "Digital teammate" is the nearest phrase but stays organizational.

---

## 2. Docebo

**What it is:** AI-powered LMS unifying learning, skills, and knowledge. URL: docebo.com

**Verbatim hero copy:**
- Hero: **"Always be upskilling. Never stop learning."**
- Subhead: **"Spot skill gaps. Personalize training. Let agents do the work. One AI platform to turn learning into impact for employees, customers, and beyond."**
- Product taglines: **"AI agents that do real work"** (AgentHub); **"AI copilot for smarter search, admin support, and actionable insights"**; **"Build and deploy no-code agents that run autonomously"**

**AgentHub product page (2026), verbatim:**
- **"Agents that don't just assist, they do the work"**
- **"Say what you need. Watch it run."**
- **"Your agent reasons, decides, and acts on its own — surfacing insights, nudging learners, escalating when needed."**
- Use-case examples: **"Review overdue compliance and email employees direction with a customized reminder"**; **"Map an employee's skills to internal roles and recommend a learning journey"**; **"Turn any document or URL into a ready-to-publish assessment in minutes"**
- Launched at Inspire 2026 (April 21, 2026), GA Fall 2026. Press framing: agents are **"not chatbots"** but **"agents that reason, decide, and act."**
- "In the flow of work" equivalent: **"Learning where your people already work"** / **"surfaces the right content in the right context"**

**Story frame:** Skills gaps are the enemy; the platform spots them and dispatches autonomous agents to close them. Shift from "tool you operate" to "agents that run on their own."

**Emotional/strategic angle:** Autonomy and offload — **"Let agents do the work," "Watch it run."** Relief-from-drudgery for admins; competence/continuous-growth for learners.

**Buyer:** No explicit role-targeting copy on the homepage (no CHRO/CLO callouts). Sells horizontally to L&D/admin function via capability, not title.

**1:1 individual companion?** No. Explicitly workflow/org-level (compliance triage, skill-gap flags, campaigns). No individual change-adoption guide.

---

## 3. WorkRamp

**What it is:** AI-first LMS for employee, partner, and customer learning/enablement. URL: workramp.com

**Verbatim hero copy:**
- Hero: **"The AI-First LMS for High-Performing Teams"**
- Subhead: **"Built to power next-gen employee, partner, and customer learning."**
- Tagline: **"The AI-First LMS to Power Every Learning Experience"**

**AI language, verbatim:**
- **"WorkRamp AI takes you from task mode to strategy mode"** — full line: **"letting WorkRamp handle the tactical work, so you can focus on designing and delivering training at scale that's targeted, relevant, and impactful."**
- **"AI-Powered Personalized Learning"**; **"Accelerate Content Creation With AI"**; **"AI Simulations to Accelerate Field Readiness"**; **"AI role plays and coaching"**
- Learner-facing AI Assistant (in Guides): **"an on-demand learning assistant... that acts as a responsive tutor, providing instant answers, simplifying complex concepts, and offering interactive practice tools to ensure learners progress with confidence"**

**Story frame:** The L&D pro is stuck in tactical busywork; AI absorbs the tactics so the human moves up to strategy. Human-empowerment ("task mode → strategy mode") more than autonomous agents.

**Emotional/strategic angle:** Aspiration + relief for the practitioner — reclaim your time, become strategic. "AI-first" as identity/badge. Field-readiness (sales-enablement flavor).

**Buyer:** Enablement and L&D practitioners (testimonials: "Sr. Instructional Designer, L&D," "L&D Specialist"). No C-level titles in headers — targets the **Head of Enablement / L&D practitioner** tier, not the CLO boardroom.

**1:1 individual companion?** Partially, but as a **tutor**, not a change-companion. The in-Guide AI Assistant is the most learner-personal ("responsive tutor... progress with confidence"), yet scoped to answering questions inside a course — not walking someone through adopting a specific new system.

---

## 4. Absorb LMS

**What it is:** AI-powered LMS with the "Aura" agent suite. URL: absorblms.com

**Verbatim hero copy:**
- Hero: **"The AI-powered LMS that actually knows your business"**
- Subhead: **"Personalized for every learner. Built into every workflow."**

**Absorb Aura (2026), verbatim:**
- **"Aura is your elite team of learning and admin agents, a powerful force multiplier that elevates every learner, manager, and admin."**
- **"Built into your AI-powered LMS, Aura delivers real-time guidance where work happens."**
- **"Aura Learn"** — answers learner questions from their assigned courses; **"When learners need a refresher or fast answer mid-task, Aura Learn pulls it"**
- **"Aura Create turns your updated document into a draft course in under an hour"**
- **"Aura Admin Assist handles your team's platform questions inside the app"**
- Personalization: **"Match training to each person's role, goals, and skill gaps"**; **"Auto-assign based on role, department, location, goals, & skill gaps"**
- In-flow: **"Built into every workflow"**; **"Learning-in-the-flow of work"**

**Story frame:** The LMS "actually knows your business," and Aura acts as a "force multiplier" team that elevates all three personas (learner, manager, admin). Emphasis on real-time, in-workflow guidance.

**Emotional/strategic angle:** Empowerment via multiplication — **"elite team," "force multiplier."** Confidence and relevance ("actually knows your business," personalized to each person). Warmer/more human-branded (named agent "Aura") than the enterprise players.

**Buyer:** HR, L&D, compliance, sales/product, customer success teams (Solutions nav). Team/function-targeted rather than a single named C-title.

**1:1 individual companion?** Closest of the four in tone — "elevates every learner," "real-time guidance where work happens," personalized to each person — but Aura is still a **suite of role-based agents (Learn/Create/Admin Assist)**, framed as a team-level force multiplier, not a single personal companion that walks an individual through adopting a specific change or system.

---

## Cross-cutting takeaways for positioning

1. **Convergent 2025–2026 language:** everyone shifted from "AI features" to **"AI agents"** in the last year (Cornerstone "system of agents," Docebo AgentHub, Absorb Aura, WorkRamp "AI-first"). The word "agent" is now table stakes, not differentiation.
2. **Shared enemy = admin drudgery + skill gaps.** All four sell offload ("let agents do the work," "task mode to strategy mode," "force multiplier"). The frame is efficiency for the L&D/admin function.
3. **Buyer skews to the function/CLO, not the individual.** Cornerstone = CLO/exec; WorkRamp/Docebo/Absorb = L&D/enablement practitioner tier. The employee is the object of the system, rarely the customer.
4. **"In the flow of work"** is used almost identically by Cornerstone, Docebo, and Absorb — it's a commodity phrase now.
5. **The white space:** a **personal, 1:1 AI companion that a single employee owns and that guides them through adopting a specific change or new system** is not claimed by any of them. Their agents serve the org and the L&D team; NanoShellano's individual-first, change-adoption companion sits outside this pattern.

**Sources:** cornerstoneondemand.com; Cornerstone HR Tech 2025 + Workforce AI press releases (May 2026); docebo.com + AgentHub product page + Inspire 2026 launch (Apr 2026); workramp.com + Help Center; absorblms.com + Aura pages (May 2026).
